raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With data-parallel attention and a non-loopback `--dist-init-addr`, the data-parallel controller binds its worker-facing ZMQ sockets on a host-reachable address so that the other nodes can connect. Those sockets decode pickle-wrapped payloads, so anything that can reach the port can push a payload at them (CVE-2026-93034, GHSA-w4hv-c72g-pqx6). Today nothing restricts who may connect.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: new `SGLANG_ZMQ_ALLOWED_PEERS`, a comma-separated list of peer IP addresses admitted by TCP-bound IPC sockets. Unset or empty admits every peer, which is today's behaviour.
- `python/sglang/srt/utils/network.py`: `restrict_zmq_peers(context, socket)` starts one ZAP `ThreadAuthenticator` per `zmq.Context` (libzmq allows a single ZAP handler per context, so sockets created from the same context share it), allows the configured addresses, and sets `zap_domain` on the socket so that libzmq vets NULL-mechanism connections. Must run before the socket binds; a no-op when the allowlist is unset. `get_zmq_socket` applies it to every TCP bind (random port and explicit endpoint). `get_zmq_socket_on_host` gains `restrict_peers=False`, off by default because disaggregation sockets accept peers from other jobs.
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py` and `python/sglang/srt/ray/data_parallel_controller.py`: the controller's worker PUSH sockets pass `restrict_peers=True`.
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/load_snapshot.py`: `ZmqShmLoadSnapshotReader` restricts peers when its endpoint is `tcp://`.

IPv6 entries may be written in any valid form; each is normalized to the compressed form that libzmq reports for a peer address, so `2001:DB8:0:0::1` matches a peer at `2001:db8::1`.

A multi-node deployment sets the variable to the addresses of its own nodes before launching every node, for example `SGLANG_ZMQ_ALLOWED_PEERS=10.0.0.1,10.0.0.2`. Single-node serving, serving without data-parallel attention and disaggregation traffic are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to scheduling, model execution or outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: with the variable unset the only addition is one empty-tuple check per socket bind; with it set, libzmq's ZAP check runs once per connection.

Functional check on this head with real sockets (pyzmq 27.2.0, libzmq 4.3.5): a PUSH client at the loopback address is delivered to a PULL socket from `get_zmq_socket` when the allowlist is unset, empty, or contains `127.0.0.1` (also when listed in long-form IPv6 company), and is dropped when the allowlist names only another address; the same holds for an explicit `tcp://` endpoint; `get_zmq_socket_on_host` keeps admitting any peer unless `restrict_peers=True`, which then drops a non-member and admits a member. `isort`, `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `codespell` at the repository's pinned versions pass on the five files.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -366,6 +366,8 @@ class Envs:
     SGLANG_USE_PICKLE_IPC = EnvBool(True)
     # Log top-level PickleWrapper frames unwrapped on msgpack IPC decode.
     SGLANG_LOG_PICKLE_IPC_OBJECTS = EnvBool(False)
+    # Comma-separated peer IPs admitted by TCP-bound IPC sockets; empty admits all.
+    SGLANG_ZMQ_ALLOWED_PEERS = EnvTuple(tuple())
     SGLANG_USE_MESSAGE_QUEUE_BROADCASTER = EnvBool(True)
     SGLANG_TCP_STORE_PORT = EnvInt(29600)
     # Base port hint for ephemeral sockets (ZMQ, SHM broadcaster, etc.).

@@ -53,7 +53,7 @@
 
 from sglang.srt.environ import envs
 from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel, get_serving
-from sglang.srt.utils.network import is_zmq_endpoint_ipv6
+from sglang.srt.utils.network import is_zmq_endpoint_ipv6, restrict_zmq_peers
 
 logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 
@@ -541,6 +541,8 @@ def __init__(self, endpoint: str, shm_path: str, dp_size: int):
             self._socket.setsockopt(_zmq.IPV6, 1)
         self._socket.setsockopt(_zmq.LINGER, 0)
         self._socket.setsockopt(_zmq.CONFLATE, 1)
+        if endpoint.startswith("tcp://"):
+            restrict_zmq_peers(self._ctx, self._socket)
         self._socket.bind(endpoint)
 
         self._endpoint = endpoint

@@ -114,7 +114,7 @@ def launch_dp_attention_schedulers(
         worker_ports = []
         for dp_rank in range(get_parallel().num_dp_ranks):
             worker_port, worker_socket = get_zmq_socket_on_host(
-                self.context, zmq.PUSH, host=self.rank0_node_ip
+                self.context, zmq.PUSH, host=self.rank0_node_ip, restrict_peers=True
             )
             worker_ports.append(worker_port)
             self.workers[dp_rank] = worker_socket

@@ -5,15 +5,22 @@
 import os
 import random
 import socket
+import threading
 import time
 from dataclasses import dataclass
 from typing import Optional, Tuple, Union
 
 import psutil
 import zmq
+from zmq.auth.thread import ThreadAuthenticator
 
 logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 
+# libzmq allows one ZAP handler per context, so sockets created from the same
+# context share an authenticator. Keyed by `zmq.Context.underlying`.
+_zmq_authenticators: dict[int, ThreadAuthenticator] = {}
+_zmq_authenticators_lock = threading.Lock()
+
 
 def get_open_port() -> int:
     from sglang.srt.environ import envs
@@ -222,10 +229,33 @@ def bind_port(port):
     return try_bind_socket(port=port, listen=True)
 
 
+def restrict_zmq_peers(context: zmq.Context, socket: zmq.Socket) -> None:
+    """Reject TCP peers outside `SGLANG_ZMQ_ALLOWED_PEERS` (CVE-2026-93034).
+
+    Must be called before `socket` binds. No-op when the allowlist is unset.
+    """
+    from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+
+    peers = envs.SGLANG_ZMQ_ALLOWED_PEERS.get()
+    if not peers:
+        return
+    with _zmq_authenticators_lock:
+        if context.underlying not in _zmq_authenticators:
+            auth = ThreadAuthenticator(context)
+            auth.start()
+            # ZAP compares the peer address as a string; libzmq formats it
+            # the same way as `ipaddress` (compressed, lowercase).
+            auth.allow(*(ipaddress.ip_address(p).compressed for p in peers))
+            _zmq_authenticators[context.underlying] = auth
+    # ZAP only vets NULL-mechanism connections when a domain is set.
+    socket.zap_domain = b"sglang"
+
+
 def get_zmq_socket_on_host(
     context: zmq.Context,
     socket_type: zmq.SocketType,
     host: Optional[str] = None,
+    restrict_peers: bool = False,
 ) -> Tuple[int, zmq.Socket]:
     """Create and configure a ZeroMQ socket.
 
@@ -236,12 +266,16 @@ def get_zmq_socket_on_host(
             "127.0.0.1" (localhost-only) to avoid exposing unauthenticated
             sockets to the network (CVE-2026-3060). Callers that need
             cross-machine reachability must pass an explicit host.
+        restrict_peers: Apply `restrict_zmq_peers`. Off by default because
+            disaggregation sockets accept peers from other jobs.
 
     Returns:
         Tuple of (port, socket) where port is the randomly assigned TCP port.
     """
     socket = context.socket(socket_type)
     config_socket(socket, socket_type)
+    if restrict_peers:
+        restrict_zmq_peers(context, socket)
     if host is None:
         host = "127.0.0.1"
     if is_valid_ipv6_address(host):
@@ -420,6 +454,7 @@ def get_zmq_socket(
     if endpoint is None:
         # Bind to random TCP port
         config_socket(socket, socket_type)
+        restrict_zmq_peers(context, socket)
         port = socket.bind_to_random_port("tcp://*")
         return port, socket
     else:
@@ -429,6 +464,8 @@ def get_zmq_socket(
         config_socket(socket, socket_type)
 
         if bind:
+            if endpoint.startswith("tcp://"):
+                restrict_zmq_peers(context, socket)
             socket.bind(endpoint)
         else:
             socket.connect(endpoint)
